newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-SMALLEST TEAM ONE OF BEST AT PAN PACIFICS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SMALLEST TEAM ONE OF BEST AT PAN PACIFICS.

text.p: The smallest team at the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships is also one of the best.
Claudia Poll is the sole member of the Costa Rican team and on Tuesday swamped the field in the women's 400 metres freestyle to win her second gold medal of the meet.
That is the same number as hosts Japan after three days of competition. Only the United States with 52 swimmers and 13 golds and Australia with 32 swimmers and seven golds have won more.
Poll's win in the 400 followed her superb performance in the 200 on Sunday when she glided to the third-best time ever of one minute 57.48 seconds in that distance.
"I think she has the best stroke in freestyle at the moment," her coach Francisco Rivas said. "Her technique is excellent."
Poll was just as imposing in the 400, winning in 4:06.56, the best time since the great Janet Evans of the United States swam 4:05.85 in 1993.
While Poll trains hard, getting up early to swim from 3.30 a.m. to 6.00 and then again from 3.30 to 6.30 in the afternoon, she and Rivas take a more casual approach to race strategy.
On Tuesday, they flipped a coin to decide how to race the 400.
"I wanted her to go out really strong in the first 200 and she didn't," said Rivas, who lost the toss.
Poll said she may have been able to go faster in the 200 if there had been anyone to challenge her.
"There was no one to push me," said Poll, who finished more than three seconds ahead of Chin's Le Jingyi.
Only Germany's world-record holder Franziska Van Almsick, in 1:56.78, and China's Lu Bin, in 1:56.89, have better times than Poll.
Both marks were set at the Rome world championships in 1994, and one month later Lu was suspended for two years after testing positive for anabolic steriods.
Poll, who won the 200 at the Atlanta Olympics, set world short-course records in both the 200 and 400 at the world championships in April in Sweden.
Rivas has coached the 24-year-old Poll for 17 years, and also took Poll's older sister Sylvia to a bronze medal in the 200 freestyle at the Seoul Olympics.
He said Poll was gearing up for the world championships in Perth in January. "As you can see from her time in the 200 free, she's ready for the worlds now."

Poll will go to Sydney at the end of August to compete in a so-called "skins" event which will also include Ireland's triple Olympic gold medalist Michelle Smith and Australian stars Susan O'Neill and Samantha Riley.
Smith won the 400 in Atlanta while Poll finished fifth.

"It will be very interesting," Rivas said. Under the "skins" rules, swimmers in each event compete in a series of elimination races until just one competitor is left. The 12 events carry total prize money of about $75,000.
Rivas said Poll's exploits had made her a hero in soccer-mad Costa Rica.
"People in Costa Rica love soccer, but they talk about Claudia," he said.
